page: Microsoft Azure E32-16ds_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine utilizing a constrained vCPU configuration from the Edsv4 series. Built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via Microsoft Hyper-V, the server is powered by an Intel Xeon Platinum 8272CL processor clocked at 2.6 GHz. It provides 16 dedicated virtual CPUs across 8 physical cores with two threads per core. The processor features 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a 35 MB shared L3 cache, with instruction support that includes AVX, AVX-512F, and AVX-512 VNNI.

The primary architectural distinction of this instance is its high memory density. It is provisioned with 256.0 GB of RAM, equating to 16.0 GB per vCPU, which significantly surpasses standard memory-to-core ratios. Local ephemeral storage is bundled directly with the hardware, offering a 1288 GB local solid-state drive (SSD) suitable for swap, paging, temporary files, and scratch space. The server does not include dedicated graphics processing units (0 GPUs) and does not come with complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results demonstrate steady mid-tier capability across computing, memory throughput, and database routines. In CPU evaluations, the instance achieved a stress-ng single-core score of 1414.2 and a multi-core score of 14893.47, alongside a Geekbench multi-core score of 7729.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 15944.59. Memory bandwidth reaches 830.88 GB/sec for small cached blocks, with large-block uncached read and write bandwidth at 69.79 GB/sec and 42.55 GB/sec, respectively. In caching and database testing, it logged 13.8 million Redis SET operations per second and a PassMark database operations score of 5436.86. Medium (7B) model LLM prompt processing registered on the lower end at 24.46 tokens/sec, reflecting limits on non-GPU compute for language models.

This instance delivers qualitative cost efficiency for organizations requiring high RAM capacity without the licensing overhead of full core counts. By offering 256 GB on only 16 vCPUs, it minimizes per-core software licensing expenses for software like enterprise relational databases. Best-fit workloads include in-memory databases, large Redis or Memcached clusters, medium-scale transactional relational databases (RDBMS), data warehousing, ETL tasks, and memory-intensive analytics pipelines.

Powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor at 2.6 GHz, it provides 16 vCPUs (8 physical cores) alongside 256.0 GB of RAM, yielding an elevated 16.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include an integrated 1288 GB local SSD for temporary storage, with no discrete GPUs included. Benchmarks position the instance in the middle tier across typical server tasks, showing 13.8 million Redis SET operations per second, a Geekbench multi-core score of 7729.0, and 69.79 GB/sec in large-block uncached read memory bandwidth.
